One of the ways my deckbuilding has changed over time is a willingness to
accept and embrace redundancy in cards I really want to have come up but
are only worthwhile in small numbers.  If I have a Ravnos deck that needs
stealth (and I do, BTW ;-) ), I REALLY want Fortune Teller Shop to come up.
Used to be, I'd throw one in figuring it was unique and grouse a lot when it
didn't show.  Now, I throw in 3 or 4 (or 5 or 6) and discard the extras.  (It
also really pisses the shit out of someone who took the time and trouble to
Arson the first one.  Or even better, Sudden Reverse it when I'm holding
another one in my hand.)

I'd happily stick 6 Gift of Baloney into a deck wanting 3 to turn up.  Actually,
I might put 8 in.  The others might never show up anyway unless I have one of
those games I draw the whole deck.

Fred

Well, any time you site next to a deck with intercept, - 1/2 to 1/3 the time
IME - you're not going to get out your weapons and your deck is just going to
die unless you can cough up a GoB with almost every equip.  It doesn't even
need to be the intercept wall Fred is worried about - even with light intercept
your opponent will have the sense to pick off your equips.  If you don't have
that problem, it's a *free* offensive untap.  You can say it's just my
preference that my deck isn't shut down 1/3 the time and that I use free
offensive untaps - but if you can find somebody who prefers to have their deck
shut down frequently and eshews free untaps, let me know where they live so I
can play against them in a tournament.

>> >Engling Fury?

>Sorry, I'm still missing your previous point: which commons are
>hindered?

Directly, any Spiritus card which costs blood, which is most of them. 
Indirectly, every common Spiritus card as EF makes Ahrimannes much better and
more playable. 

I'm curious why you value EF and Unwholesome Bond so differently.   
UB will, on average, generate more blood and can also generate pool,
but it costs an action and lacks an outferior.  UB is probably a little
better, all things considered, but why such a huge difference in
rarity?
 
>> >Blessing of the Name 
>I'm still missing the "necessary in number for proper functioning
>of common cards" link.

Directly, Vengeance of Samiel and Sword of Righteousness - without BotN they
are used later in the game, do less damage, and are harder to use (less
intercept).  Indirectly, every common Valeren card, as BotN makes the !Sal much
better and more playable.

IMO, without the semi-power rares, I don't think either the !Sal or the
Ahrimanes are worth the considerable trouble consequent to their tightly
limited crypts and difficult multiclan use.  All the BL clans are hard to 
use; you need somebig payoff to make them worth it.  In both cases, I think 
the semi-power rares would qualify, at least to the point of making a shot at
it.

I'm not sure that's exactly what Ian said.  He just suggested there were two
ways to use the card and it would take at least 20 in the deck to use it the
way I was talking about.  I don't think it's quite that high, myself.  But then,
he (and you?) may be assuming a 90-card deck, which (right offhand) probably

occasional turn without one.  Ultimately, there's usually only so much my opponents
can do in a single turn.  I'm counting on not being so close to the edge that
one turn of no Blessing is not usually going to oust me.  And once it happens,
you can wait and collect up a couple before starting in again, I suspect - unless
you've been keeping a vote deck at bay with the intercept or something.

> because it's just a +1 stealth action that someone will eventually decide to
> block.

If people start doing that to you, you blow through the cards faster.  I think
to make it work, you're going to have to have effective combat working, too.
And if so, they won't block too many Blessings.  If not, then you're probably
in a losing position anyway.

> I find that the surprise "All my guys untap and bleed or Rush, whatever
> they didn't do earlier this turn" at key points is quite effective.

It can be.  Pulsing and Bleeding in the same turn is always strong.

Fred

> "Joshua Duffin" <jtduffin@yahoo.com> wrote in message

[on whether unwholesome bond would've been a better rare
than coagulated entity]

> > heh, I'd actually disagree here.  The Blood Brothers vamps
> > are expensive enough that Unwholesome Bond seems pretty
> > important to making them usable, even if combat is what
> > you want to do with them otherwise.
>
> Expensive? How so? They're discipline spread rocks! (Pot and For?
> Hell... I would believe any vampire withsuch a discipline combo should
> cost another half pool... if half pools existed... Course I feel the
> same about Obf and Dom)

Expensive in that even in the Chicago circle they all
cost 5 pool (except Tom), and in Torrance they're 6
each.  That's *really* expensive for a combat clan,
especially one that can't use 2nd Tradition (or similar).
Successful rush-combat decks (IME) use weenies, like
no vampires over 4-cap and an average cap of no more
than 3.  You can't really make a Blood Bros deck that
has an average cap any lower than 4.5, and 6 is gonna
be more typical.

So, if you don't use Unwholesome Bond, you're either
gonna only get out 2-3 vampires per game (assuming
that you're playing against competent players who will
be putting enough effort into reducing your pool that
you can't afford to spend more than 12-18 pool on
vampires), or else you'll have to spend your deckspace
on Blood Dolls and other ways to refill your vampires.
(The other drawback of not using Unwholesome Bond is
that your vampires come out quite slowly since they're
all too large to be transferred out in a single turn
(Tom again notwithstanding).  That's why it's so good:
it not only saves you pool, it also speeds you up so
you can start doing stuff earlier on.)

I'd also disagree that their discipline spread is *that*
good - yeah, Potence and Fortitude sound great on paper,
but they don't focus on those skills narrowly enough to
make them some kind of uber-great Pot/For combat clan:
only one of the ten Bros has POT/FOR; only one of the
Chicago circle has superior of either, and she doesn't
have *any* of the other (Terry, with POT/no fortitude);
only two more of Torrance (besides POT/FOR Karl) have
a superior of Potence or Fortitude.  Basically, they
spend a *lot* of their discipline points on Sanguinus,
and ignoring that to just use their Potence and Fortitude
looks to me like a seriously losing plan.

> > So is
> > Darkling Trickery at superior Myt, but at inferior it's
> > general-purpose enough that it might make a better common
> > than, say, Absorb the Mind.  Or not, but its inferior
> > definitely makes more sense at common than rare.  :-)
>
> Whose inferior? Darkling or Absorb?

Well, both, really, but I meant Darkling - maneuver or
press is like Flash and a very useful effect for any
combat discipline (which Mytherceria is, at least to
some extent).

Absorb the Mind's inf Myt level is also pretty general;
steal one blood, ranged, isn't bad, and is the same
as inferior Theft of Vitae.  The superior only works
if there's a discipline master to steal, but the inf
is always usable which makes it (IMO) a pretty reasonable
common card.


Josh
